task.description: Rework 4 of the ISS-0427 design: fix two remaining defects before merge. (1) LIKE INCLUDING ALL renames indexes, so the parity check's own deliberate structural-not-name comparison is, by construction, blind to a clone whose indexes are structurally correct but differently named -- which breaks Ecto's unique_constraint/3 name-based error mapping and turns 7/8 remaining suite failures into raw Ecto.ConstraintError instead of clean 409s. Settle the mechanism (rename vs recreate vs no-LIKE-indexes), the primary-key/constraint-backed-index interaction, and the corrected parity check. (2) ISSUE-FIXER's crash-safety finding: build_template!/0's CREATE SCHEMA commits unconditionally outside any transaction, so a later failure leaves a permanently empty, undetected template wedging every future ensure_template!/0 call in that partition database; also the MINOR upsert gap on the throwaway Registration insert.

result.summary:
Design updated in place, four new sections added to lib/letflow/design/iss0427-tenant-test-schema-template-clone.md (now 2196 lines): section 0.6 (index/constraint NAME parity finding + mechanism decision), section 0.7 (build_template!/0 crash-safety finding + mechanism decision), plus the corresponding mechanism-step and parity-check edits at their established locations (section 2.3 step 3.5, section 2.3 steps 0-6 restructured, section 3.2 dimension 4(b)), plus INV-7/INV-8, OQ-7, and updated section 11 acceptance-criteria rows. No implementation code added -- verified by inspection, only prose, SQL fragments quoted as evidence of probe results, and @spec-style signatures.

MECHANISM CHOSEN FOR INDEX NAMES: option (b), ALTER INDEX ... RENAME TO, not option (a) drop-and-recreate-from-catalog and not option (c) abandon LIKE INCLUDING INDEXES. Verified directly against a psql probe in letflow_dev modelling the real users-table shape (pkey, plain unique expression index, partial unique index, named UNIQUE table constraint): (1) LIKE INCLUDING ALL preserves users_pkey unchanged (a coincidence of Postgres's own default <table>_pkey naming convention independently regenerating the same string at both migration-build time and LIKE-clone time, not special-case logic -- so the fix needs no PK special-casing, it naturally no-ops on the one pair whose names already match); (2) every other index (plain, partial, and a named UNIQUE constraint's backing index) gets Postgres's generic auto-name (users_username_index -> users_lower_idx, users_external_identity_partial_index -> users_external_realm_external_id_idx, users_username_uq -> users_username_key); (3) ALTER INDEX ... RENAME TO on a constraint-backed index renames the OWNING pg_constraint row atomically in the same statement -- verified by querying pg_constraint before/after, conname changed together with the index, no separate ALTER TABLE ... RENAME CONSTRAINT needed, no window where the two names could disagree; (4) after renaming all three non-pkey indexes back to their template names, a duplicate insert raised 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint "users_username_index"' -- the template's own name, verbatim, confirming the fix produces exactly the string Ecto's unique_constraint/3 needs to match. COST, measured not assumed: ALTER INDEX RENAME cost 1.0-9.8ms per index (pure catalog metadata update, no index rebuild); option (a) (DROP INDEX + CREATE UNIQUE INDEX from the template's indexdef) cost 1.5ms+30.1ms=~31.6ms on the identical index -- a 3-30x higher cost for an identical structural result, because CREATE INDEX physically rebuilds from a table scan even on an empty table, and (a) still would not recreate the pg_constraint row for a constraint-backed index without a further ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX statement (b) doesn't need. Option (c) (build every index from scratch, no LIKE INCLUDING INDEXES) rejected without a fresh measurement beyond what (a) already establishes as the floor -- it would replace ISS-0427's whole one-CREATE-TABLE-per-table premise with ~105 individual CREATE INDEX statements (the real schema's own index count, cited in section 0), forfeiting the 2.0-2.5x win this issue exists to capture. All probe schemas (probe_tpl/probe_clone/probe_tpl2/probe_clone2/probe_tpl3/probe_clone3) dropped clone-before-template and confirmed gone via pg_namespace (0 rows) both mid-sequence and at the end, before this document was written.

MECHANISM STEP ADDED (design section 2.3, new step 3.5 in clone_tenant_schema!/1, between the existing LIKE loop and FK re-add): per table, query pg_indexes on both template and just-created clone, pair by structural indexdef (schema-qualifier-normalized AND own-name-stripped -- reusing the exact rework-3 dimension-4 technique already established, not reinvented), then ALTER INDEX RENAME every pair whose names differ.

PARITY CHECK CORRECTED (design section 3.2, dimension 4): split into two mandatory, non-subsuming sub-assertions -- (a) structure, unchanged from rework 3 (name-blind, multiset-of-normalized-indexdef comparison, this is what avoids reintroducing the rework-3 false-fail); (b) NEW -- after pairing by (a), assert indexname is IDENTICAL between the paired reference and candidate index. Ordering is what prevents (b) from reintroducing the false-fail (a) fixed: pair first by structure (name-blind), THEN assert name equality on the now-paired objects (structure-blind) -- never a single combined name-and-structure match that would have to pick a matching key up front. This is the check that would have caught the post-merge defect at build/clone-test time instead of surfacing as an unrelated-looking Ecto.ConstraintError seven application tests away. Same correction noted as applying to dimension 11 (pg_statistic_ext) for the same embedded-name reason, consistent with the existing rework-3 note there.

THE ASSUMPTION THIS DESIGN MISSED, stated explicitly per the dispatch's item 4 (design section 0.6, opening paragraphs, and new INV-7): index/constraint names are load-bearing, not cosmetic, because Ecto.Changeset.unique_constraint/3 and foreign_key_constraint/3 resolve a Postgres constraint violation back to a changeset field by matching the violating object's NAME against a :name option -- so 'structurally equivalent' (which section 3.2 dimension 4 already asserted correctly) is necessary but not sufficient; the design never stated this until now, which is why the parity check could pass a clone that then crashed the application.

CRASH-SAFETY FIX (design section 0.7): chosen mechanism is atomic build-then-rename-into-place, not detect-and-repair. Detect-and-repair was rejected as the PRIMARY mechanism (not fully preventive -- a concurrent caller could still observe the broken half-state in the window before repair runs, and it requires the repair path itself to be reliable and non-recursive) though it remains implicitly available as a manual recovery for a genuinely stuck database. Atomic build-then-rename: build the ENTIRE template (schema, tables, indexes+renames, FKs, sequences, triggers, seed data -- the complete, unchanged-in-substance section-2.3 sequence) under a freshly randomized staging schema name (tenant_template_build_<hex>), and only after the self-check has PASSED against the staging schema, issue ALTER SCHEMA <staging> RENAME TO tenant_template -- a single catalog-level statement, no table/index rebuild. Consequence, stated as new INV-8: the literal name 'tenant_template' can never exist in a half-built state -- it either doesn't exist yet, or it is fully built and self-check-passed, because the rename is the LAST statement in the sequence. A crash at any point before the rename leaves only harmless, inert, never-registered staging-schema debris behind, never a wedged tenant_template. This closes ISSUE-FIXER's MAJOR finding structurally rather than by adding a retry/repair loop. THE MINOR (insert_throwaway_tenant_and_registration!/1 has no upsert) is SUBSUMED by this same fix, not separately patched: once each build attempt targets a fresh randomized staging schema name, the throwaway Registration row's schema_name value is also fresh per attempt, so a stale row from a prior crashed attempt (naming ITS OWN abandoned staging schema) can never collide with a new attempt's insert -- the two rows have different schema_name values by construction. Section 2.3's step list was restructured (steps 0-6, replacing the old steps 1-4) to specify exactly which literal-'tenant_template' references become staging-schema references and which don't (clone_tenant_schema!/1's own steps are unaffected, since by the time it runs the rename has already happened).

OPEN QUESTION ADDED (OQ-7): whether TenantSchemaReaper should gain a second sweep pattern for orphaned staging schemas (tenant_template_build_*) in a long-lived, not-regularly-reset dev database -- not designed here, stated as genuinely open rather than silently assumed unnecessary, since this design's own reasoning for why it's low-risk (ephemeral per-run databases) does not fully cover a persistent local dev database, which is exactly the shape of debris ISSUE-FIXER found and ORCH's own prior probing produced.

All new probe-based claims in sections 0.6 and 0.7 are this session's own direct psql verification against letflow_dev (container letflow-2-postgres-1), not inherited from ORCH's log or ISSUE-FIXER's handoff unchecked -- the root-cause claim (LIKE renames indexes; Ecto matches by name) was verified independently via a fresh, self-built probe reproducing the exact users_username_index/users_external_identity_partial_index naming pattern cited in the dispatch, not merely re-quoted from the log.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for the rework-4 re-gate (index-name mechanism in section 0.6/2.3 step 3.5/3.2 dimension 4(b), and crash-safety mechanism in section 0.7/2.3 steps 0-6/INV-8), then to ELIXIR-DEV to implement both fixes in test/support/tenant_template.ex.
